reasoning_summary: Verified the excerpt (QI-rigidity of graphs of surface groups) step by step in order. Checked in detail: (a) the end of Prop. combinatorialize (lines 0259-0275) - the strongly-connected-component/cut-point argument and the inductive extension to a local isometry between simply connected complexes; (b) Prop. strands (0366-0443) - g^n central via exponent of Aut(K); Min(g^n)=Y x R invariant by Thm II.6.8(3); Y bounded since X is 2-ended and Y x R is convex; Y_0 nonempty via the CAT(0) centre; independence of Y_0 x R from the lift g; the dihedral computation g^n r x = r(r^{-1}g^n r)x = r g^{-n} k x = r g^{-n} x (k acts trivially on Y_0 x R since K is finite, so its R-component translation is 0), giving d(rx, g^n rx) = d(x, g^{-n}x) = |g^n| so rx in Min(g^n); Gamma-invariance of {c_{Y_1}} x R; (c) Lem. strand-classification (0460-0485) - the case split on |(K_sigma)_x| in {1,2,4} and on whether K_sigma\sigma is a circle or segment is exhaustive and each case gives the listed group; (d) Prop. quadrilaterals (0571-0598) - recomputed: length(alpha)=(b-a)/y_1, length(beta)=(b-a)/y_2, so |ln(length alpha / length beta)| = ln(y_2/y_1) = width, and each vertical leaf has length int_{y1}^{y2} dt/t = ln(y_2/y_1); the 'long side' at y=y_1 is indeed the longer one, so the long-side convention in Defn. churro-metrization (tau_core > tau_sigma_i => core is the long side) is the consistent one; (e) Lem. ratio - the flap widths |ln(tau_core/tau_sigma_i)| = |ln(bar-alpha/alpha_i)| are scale-invariant, so the clutching ratios determine the churro metric; (f) Prop. projection (1000-1023) - tripod bookkeeping |alpha_2|=|gamma_1|=|gamma_2|=|beta_2|, d(x,z) <= |alpha_1|+delta+R, minimality gives |alpha_2| <= delta+R, hence 2(delta+R); (g) Lem. lowpower - |L(n)| = n, regular action is free and transitive, class closed under products/subgroups, isomorphism determined by order; (h) Prop. clutching (1036-1117), the load-bearing argument: uniform-in-n QI constants for psi_1^{(n)} (h^n is an isometry), Q_n = g^{m_n}x' within a'/2 of the combinatorialization, m_n -> infinity, omega scales lengths by b/a so omega(bar-phi_1^{-1}(Q_n)) sits at distance m_n a' b/a from y, matching the definition of P_n, while omega'(Q_n) = g^{m_n}y' sits at distance m_n b' from y'; both are boundedly close to phi(h^n y), and since a/b > a'/b' implies b' - a'b/a > 0 the separation grows linearly in m_n, forcing a/b = a'/b'. The argument is sound. Defects found are cosmetic and non-load-bearing: line 0268 writes 'phi_n: X_n -> X_n' for X_n -> W_2; line 0973 writes d(phi(x), phi(sigma'_i)) where sigma_i is meant; line 1109 states the domain of psi_1^{(n)} as W_1 rather than N(W_1'); and, most substantively, line 1117 displays d(P_n, omega'(Q_n)) = m_n(a/b - a'/b') when the actual value is m_n(b' - a'b/a) = m_n (b b'/a)(a/b - a'/b') (e.g. a=2, b=1, a'=1, b'=1 gives the true value m_n/2 versus the displayed m_n). This is an off-by-a-positive-constant-factor slip: the quantity is still a positive multiple of m_n, which is all the contradiction requires, so it does not break the proof. No step failed in a way that invalidates the argument.
